issues.title: bun add of #HEAD leaves #HEAD in package.json and the docs don't say how to pin the commit
issues.doing: Adding rack42u as the instructions say: bun add git+file://<repository>#HEAD
issues.happened: links: package.json got "rack42u": "git+file:///...rack42u#HEAD"; the commit shows only in bun's output. chat: the skill says bun add git+ssh://...#<tag>, the trial uses git+file://<repo>#HEAD; Bun saved #HEAD in package.json, which had to be edited to the commit by hand. watcher: bun add --cwd <app> git+file:///…/rack42u#HEAD valibot -> package.json got "rack42u": "git+file:///home/zmmfly/prjs/rack42u#HEAD"; the commit appears only in the output.
issues.expected: The resolved commit pinned automatically, or the documentation saying that Bun keeps the typed ref and how to pin a commit
issues.where: getting-started.md#add-rack42u says to pin a tag or commit but gives no way to get the commit into package.json, and does not say that Bun keeps the typed ref
issues.workaround: Edited package.json by hand with the commit Bun reported. Did not read source.

sources.title: The skill's install command does not match the trial's

issues.title: Per-instance in-memory state must be module-level for snapshot/restore, and the docs don't say why
issues.doing: chat: handing the sockets to the new instance (handler.list() in snapshot, handler.restore() in restore). watcher: keeping a checker's last result and the store's reports across a hot swap.
issues.happened: chat: snapshot and restore get no access to what powerOn built, so the handler and the history map live in module variables (let handler). watcher: snapshot/restore can't reach closures made in powerOn; the agent first wrote an awkward indirection before using module-level variables.
issues.expected: Documentation saying that module-level state is the pattern and why it is safe (one Worker per instance), or a documented place for per-instance state, such as powerOn's return value or a member of ctx
issues.where: guides/devices.md 'Hooks' and '#a-device-file' (the greeter example): module-level state is shown without saying why it is safe or that snapshot/restore cannot reach powerOn's closures
issues.workaround: Module-level variables; worked in the swap. Did not read source.

sources.title: Module-level variable needed to reach the handler from snapshot
Per-instance in-memory state must be module-level for snapshot/restore

issues.title: The rack-from-code example doesn't mention the logger option to silence the log
issues.doing: Silencing the rack's console log in check.ts
issues.happened: Guessed log: "silent", which needed `as any` and was ignored; logs still printed. The agent found logger only by grepping reference/api.md.
issues.expected: An obvious option, mentioned next to the start() example
issues.where: guides/running.md 'Running a rack from code' shows start(manifest, { baseDir }) and never mentions logger

issues.title: No recipe for a check that changes a device with swap() while the rack runs
issues.doing: The check must change the handling device while the app runs
issues.happened: Docs show rack dev edits and swap(name, source?), but not whether swap(name) of an unchanged file does anything, or how a check changes a device. The agent wrote a modified copy into scratch/ and swapped to it (its relative imports must still resolve).
issues.expected: A recipe for tests of a hot swap
issues.where: guides/updates.md and the swap() row of reference/api.md
issues.workaround: Copy with a changed line, running.swap('chat','./scratch/chat-next.ts'), then running.history('chat')[0] to confirm. Did not read source.

sources.title: No example of a swap that changes the file under start()

issues.title: The skill doesn't lead to the pattern for a layout that follows a data file
issues.doing: A URL added to watch.json must get a checker without restarting the others
issues.happened: rack start/rack dev don't re-read the manifest when a file it reads changes. The skill's steps 4 and 6 don't mention running.md#a-layout-that-follows-data, which holds the pattern (start() + reload(manifest)).
issues.expected: A documented way, easy to find from the skill
issues.workaround: Wrote watcher.ts that runs start(), watches watch.json with fs.watch and calls reload(layout(...)); the app runs with `bun watcher.ts`. Did not read source.

sources.title: No documented watch mode for a layout that follows a data file under rack start

issues.title: The update record of a plug done by reload() has cause reload, which the docs don't say
issues.doing: Checking via history() that only the new checker was plugged
issues.happened: The record was { mode: "plug", cause: "reload" }; the agent expected cause: "plug".
issues.expected: cause: "plug", or documentation saying which cause a plug done by reload() has
issues.where: guides/updates.md#history lists plug as a cause and as a mode without saying that a plug done by reload() has cause reload
issues.workaround: Checked mode instead of cause. Did not read source.

sources.title: Update record cause for a plug during reload() is reload, not plug

issues.title: A baseDir outside the app can't resolve the device's packages, and the docs and error don't say so
issues.doing: Testing the device on the bench with a temporary directory in os.tmpdir() as baseDir
issues.happened: RackError: .../devices/files.ts: Cannot find package 'rack42u' imported from /tmp/files-test-iaMNfd/.rack/firmware/files-wrgg5nxe.js (code RACK_MANIFEST)
issues.expected: baseDir only says where relative paths resolve and where data goes; the docs say nothing of module resolution. Expected either that to work or the docs/error to say baseDir must lie inside the app.
issues.where: reference/api.md start options (baseDir) and guides/testing.md bench options: neither says firmware is written under <baseDir>/.rack/firmware/ and resolves imported packages from there, so baseDir must lie inside the app
issues.workaround: Used a temporary folder inside the app's scratch/ as baseDir; guessed the cause from the message and the firmware path. Did not read source.

sources.title: A bench or rack with a baseDir outside the app can't resolve the device's packages
